title: Native persistence durability and fault-model audit
capsule: read-only; no real saves touched; no ports bound; port 6500 untouched

D-106.statement: Items are never destroyed by Scion death; everything carried returns to a recoverable pool (relic pool / loot pool). Death transforms recoverability.
nativeEvidence: native/src/core.cpp:563-605 retire_instance() requeues surfaced relic/trophy candidates into pending pools at every instance boundary
native/tests/core_tests.cpp:778-819 D-109 mid-instance snapshot preserves carried items/trophies
native/tests/core_tests.cpp:821-845 recovery pools survive snapshot/restore byte-stably

D-109.statement: Logout, disconnect, or crash never loses items or progress; Scion keeps everything and returns to town on next login. Death is the only loss event.
nativeEvidence: native/src/core.cpp:1265-1291 snapshot retires active instance; surfaced candidates return to pending queues
native/src/networking.cpp:604-651 reset_world_for_new_socket() resets transient state, keeps account state, restores life
native/tests/session_tests.cpp:401-450 disconnect/restart/relogin cycle stays Ready without losing identity

headlineFinding: The native persistence seam exists and is well-tested as a library (core snapshot/restore + atomic file adapter), but it has ZERO production callers: no save trigger exists anywhere in native production code. All live profiles (ProtocolSession state, networking.hpp:161-247) are process-memory only, so a native server crash or restart silently resets every guest to a fresh deterministic profile. D-109 currently holds within a running process only.

coreSnapshotFormat.purpose: Versioned, canonical, line-oriented durable House/Scion/RNG bytes; no I/O inside the core (D-002).
coreSnapshotFormat.schemaVersionGate: kSnapshotSchemaVersion=1 (native/src/core.cpp:964); restore hard-throws on missing/mismatched version (native/src/core.cpp:1299-1301); no migration path

grammar.encoding: key=value lines, UTF-8 strings hex-encoded lower-case (native/src/core.cpp:968-996); numbers decimal; booleans 0/1; fixed field order gives byte-stable output
grammar.parsing: first-occurrence-wins duplicate keys, CRLF tolerated, blank/separator-less lines skipped (native/src/core.cpp:1079-1093)
grammar.failClosed: missing required fields throw 'missing snapshot field'; malformed numbers/booleans/hex throw with key name (native/src/core.cpp:1101-1141); collection counts capped at 1e6 (native/src/core.cpp:1143-1147)

fileAdapter.writeAtomic: temp file '<target>.tmp' -> write -> flush -> close -> MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING|WRITE_THROUGH) on Windows / rename(2) elsewhere; failure removes temp and throws (adapter.hpp:23-57)
fileAdapter.read: plain byte read; never touches .tmp leftovers (adapter.hpp:59-73)
knownGaps: No FlushFileBuffers/fsync of temp data before rename; MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH covers the metadata op only, so an OS-crash/power-loss window can leave a durably-renamed but empty/truncated target (adapter.hpp:27-35)
Fixed '.tmp' suffix: concurrent writers to one target share and clobber one temp path (adapter.hpp:25)
Crash between temp creation and rename leaves a stale .tmp that read() ignores and nothing ever cleans

atomicity.mechanism: write temp -> flush/close -> atomic replace (MoveFileExW REPLACE_EXISTING|WRITE_THROUGH on Windows because std::filesystem::rename cannot replace there; POSIX rename(2)); failed replace removes temp and throws
guarantees: no observer inside one process ever sees a half-written target (rename is atomic within the OS)
violations: OS crash / power loss before temp data reaches disk: rename can still be durable while data is not (no fsync/FlushFileBuffers of the temp stream) - adapter.hpp:27-47
concurrent writers share the single fixed .tmp path - last interleaved writer wins or both fail - adapter.hpp:25
atomicity.testsCovering: happy path write/read/replace twice (native/tests/core_tests.cpp:880-891); no failure-path or concurrency tests exist

staleDataCompatibility.policyInconsistency: three version seams with three different policies: core hard-fails (untested), chronicle v3 never checked, skilltree v2 never checked (see serializationSeams)

negativeControl.primaryStaleVersion: F-03: a realistic rollback/newer-build snapshot (schemaVersion != 1) is rejected by implemented code (core.cpp:1299-1301) yet NO current test locks the rejection. A refactor that silently accepts foreign versions would pass the entire suite.
negativeControl.secondaryPartialWrite: F-01/F-10: truncated-file rejection and concurrent-writer integrity are likewise implemented-or-designed but entirely untested; the fixed .tmp name makes F-10 a genuine torn-write vector the moment production saves land.

redRisks.risk: No production save trigger: native server holds all profiles in process memory; crash/restart loses everything silently, contradicting D-109 across process death (holds today only because native server is dev-loop scoped).
Session-layer profile (inventory, bank, quests, passive tree, chronicle, XP, lifecycle) has no serialization seam at all; wiring core snapshot() alone would persist only the small Simulation slice.
Adapter lacks fsync/FlushFileBuffers before rename: power-loss can strand a durable rename over empty/partial data.
Fixed '<target>.tmp' name: concurrent writers (server + tooling on one House file) can interleave or destroy each other's temp.
Three inconsistent stale-version policies (core hard-fail untested; chronicle v3 and skilltree v2 never validated).
sessions_ map never evicts identities: unbounded memory growth on long-lived servers.
restore() mirrors only the FIRST equipped carried item onto the live Actor; multi-equipped saves degrade the mirror (underlying Scion data intact).

smallestLockingTests: L1 (locks F-03): expect throw when restoring schemaVersion=0 and =2 rewrites of a valid snapshot
L2 (locks F-01): expect throw when truncating bytes immediately after a count line
L3 (locks F-07): appended duplicate canonical key is ignored in favor of first occurrence
L4 (locks F-10): concurrent write_atomic pairs over one disposable temp target always leave one exact payload
L5 (locks F-11): reading a missing path throws and creates nothing
L6 (successor, post-R1/R2): server-restart durability - login, mutate, restart process seam, re-login, assert profile equality; today this test CANNOT pass, which is precisely the R1 gap
